steps.thirds: A triad is three notes stacked in thirds: the root, the third and the fifth. Its color depends on the size of those thirds. A major triad has a major third, then a minor third: {c}, {e}, {g}. A minor triad has them the other way round: {c}, {eFlat}, {g}.
steps.twoColors: Count the half steps from the root to the middle note: four for major, three for minor.
steps.others: Two more stacks are possible. Two minor thirds make a diminished triad, narrow and tense: {b}, {d}, {f}. Two major thirds make an augmented triad, wide and unsettled: {c}, {e}, {gSharp}.
steps.read: On the staff the notes are stacked in thirds. Look at the accidentals, and count the half steps of each third.
steps.build: Now play them. The three notes can come in any order, together or one at a time.
steps.ear: Now with your ears. Each chord plays its notes one by one, then together.
